claims.claim: Narrative-design experts list AI game narrative failures: unconvincing or repetitive content, wrong genre, uneven quality across sessions, and a bias toward overly positive endings.
63% of game design and narrative workers say generative AI harms the industry (GDC 2026, n>2,300); positive views fell to 7%.
claims.quote: a regurgitated amalgamation of everything that's come before

claims.claim: ChatGPT-written RPG adventures land at the most ordinary text possible; the quality floor comes with an equal ceiling.
claims.source: H. Tucker Cobey, Epic Table Games, 2023-07-24
claims.quote: the most ordinary, middle-of-the-road adventure text

claims.claim: DMs Guild and DriveThruRPG refuse commercial content primarily written by AI language generators (effective 2023-07-31) while allowing tagged AI art.
claims.source: OneBookShelf policy via EN World thread
claims.quote: primarily written by AI language generators

claims.claim: Kobold Press pledges no AI-generated text in game design, framing LLM text as fine for chatbots but not for play with friends.
claims.source: Wolfgang Baur, Kobold Press 'No AI Pledge'
claims.quote: we don't use AI to generate text

claims.feature: publisher bans are ethical not qualitative
claims.claim: Paizo, Chaosium, WotC, Renegade, Stonemaier, Free League ban AI text/art on ethics and livelihood grounds; only Monte Cook Games gives a quality verdict.

claims.feature: AI RPG text stagnant and obvious
claims.claim: RPG crowdfunding backers report AI-written project text is easy to catch and has not improved in three years; human creators now fear tripping the same alarm.
claims.source: EN World, 'AI is destroying crowdfunding' (user Agamon, 2026-08-25)
claims.quote: it's been at the same level for three years

claims.claim: Letting AI draft sequels from the same source documents reproduced the first book's story beats; prose stayed 'competent but slightly mechanical' with 'not X but Y'.

claims.feature: prompt shipped in a published novel
claims.claim: A Kindle Unlimited novel (Darkhollow Academy: Year 2, June 2025) went out with an AI rewrite prompt still in the text; Amazon's AI disclosure is not shown to readers.
claims.source: Book Riot, 'Can Kindle Unlimited Survive AI?'

claims.claim: Goodreads readers flag ~296 books as obviously AI-generated on the basis of AI cover art plus stereotypical text patterns at slop-level frequency.
A human-written indie RPG was review-bombed as ChatGPT slop because the story 'felt artificial'; reader tells fire on human work too.
There is no hard evidence that chatbots use more em dashes than professional human writers; their prevalence in AI output reflects training on human prose.
claims.quote: how reliant the AI companies are on the human writers
claims.page: Stop AI-Shaming Our Precious, Kindly Em Dashes—Please

claims.claim: The em dash was Emily Dickinson's signature mark, restored by later editors after publishers stripped it; treating it as an AI tell confuses the tool with the intent behind it.
claims.quote: Machines use it because great writers always have.
claims.page: The Em Dash Is Not an AI Tell

claims.claim: Google Books Ngram data show em dash frequency in published books has stayed high for centuries, so ChatGPT is mirroring professional convention rather than exhibiting a machine signature.
claims.quote: There is no simple formula for detecting AI writing.
claims.page: In Defence of the em dash

claims.claim: An AP Stylebook editor confirms em dashes are ubiquitous in professional journalism and predate AI; avoiding them to dodge suspicion lets machines dictate human style in a feedback loop.
claims.page: AI's Assault on the Em Dash Should Worry All Writers
